title: What if you were the last doctor on Earth?

hook.narration: You're the last doctor on Earth. Nobody is coming.

visual.v1: dark ward at night; ONE bed lit by the surgical lamp cone (the only light source); title ON frame-0; one heartbeat pulse in the glow; hero doctor small at the bed rail

scenes.narration: One patient is still breathing in your dark ward.

visual.v1: tighter on the bed: the sheet rises and falls twice (breathing); the doctor's hand lands on the rail late in the line; ECG teal line steady

scenes.narration: The blood bank keeps for a few weeks. Then it's empty.

visual.v1: the blood cart: three blood bags hang labelled; they grey out one by one as the line ends (countable, colour cue visible)

scenes.narration: Insulin survives only in the cold. The power died last night.

visual.v1: insulin cooler open: vials on an ice pack, frost breath; the ward's back ceiling lights flicker and die on 'power'

scenes.narration: Triage is simple now. Save the ones you can reach.

visual.v1: corridor of empty beds receding in the dark; two beds grey out, one stays warm-lit; doctor at the doorway with a clipboard

scenes.narration: Your hands remember what the machines used to know.

visual.v1: close on the bed: patient monitor + ventilator ghost-fade out of frame; the doctor's gloved hands flex, ready
VISUAL-ONLY: THE OPERATION — under the lamp, five stitches close the wound left to right, each with a tick ring; the last lands u>=0.8; doctor leaning in, ECG steady

scenes.narration: Out there, whole towns are still waiting for help.

visual.v1: pull back through the ward window: a dark town skyline at night, a handful of lit windows, one road out

scenes.narration: The last supply truck never made it.

visual.v1: the road at night: ONE truck dominates the frame, hood up, headlights dim to dark as the line lands

scenes.narration: You mark every town you couldn't reach.

visual.v1: a paper map on the desk: labelled town dots; the pen X-marks land one after another while the camera slides right

scenes.narration: At dawn, you still have one patient, one job.

visual.v1: the window turns gold; first warm light fills the ward (G9 pivot); doctor silhouette at the window, patient bed behind

scenes.narration: Because someone always has to stitch.

visual.v1: quiet close-up: the doctor steady at the bedside, hand on the sheet; ECG steady teal; no chip - the line lands alone

scenes.narration: So you wash your hands, check the lamp, and begin again.

visual.v1: loop scene: the hook's wide ward frame; water glints off the washed hands; the lamp flickers back ON; STAMP: SOMEONE ALWAYS HAS TO STITCH

sources.premise: What-if premise (no factual claim beyond the counterfactual); register = compassion + dread + duty per research/video-notes/alignment-emotion-whatif.md (9/10 alignment).
sources.fda_aabb: FDA/CBER + AABB standards: stored red blood cells remain transfusable for weeks depending on anticoagulant (platelets only days). Narration keeps it qualitative: 'a few weeks'.
sources.who_insulin: WHO / MedlinePlus storage guidance: insulin must stay refrigerated (~2-8 deg C); heat exposure degrades potency. Narration keeps it qualitative: 'only in the cold'.
sources.atls: ATLS / START triage doctrine (American College of Surgeons): in mass-casualty conditions, treat the survivable - greatest good for the greatest number. Narration: 'save the ones you can reach'.
sources.imprint: Deliberate callback to #0006's closer word ('stitch') - the channel-imprint stitch motif.
